findings: The candidate directly answers all four frozen HashMap/HashTable source variants and normalizes the Java type name to java.util.Hashtable without changing the source intent.

Java SE 21 documents HashMap as unsynchronized with null-key/null-value support and Hashtable as synchronized with non-null keys/values; the candidate preserves those observable API contracts without turning implementation details into universal rules.

Java SE 21 explicitly recommends ConcurrentHashMap when a thread-safe highly-concurrent map is desired, so the candidate's modern-selection guidance is primary-source supported rather than a generic performance slogan.

The Collections.synchronizedMap traversal caveat in the candidate is supported by the Java SE 21 Collections contract: traversal of collection views requires manual synchronization on the returned map.

OpenJDK 21 GA confirms the version-bound implementation distinction used by the candidate: HashMap contains tree-bin machinery while Hashtable retains synchronized legacy-table/rehash structure; the answer correctly keeps these details secondary to the cross-version API comparison.

The answer explicitly rejects two common correctness mistakes: treating HashMap fail-fast behavior as synchronization and treating per-method Hashtable synchronization as automatic atomicity for arbitrary multi-call business invariants.
